name: captive fairies

attributes.attribute: vanishes into the lake on regaining her swanskin

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Captive fairies form an Irish mythological theme. Certain kinds of fairies could be caught, though doing so took effort. Leprechauns could be caught by grasping their small shoulders. They used every trick to escape. They seldom let their hoarded gold pass to anyone else. A fairy woman who took swan form on a lake could be caught if someone carried off the swanskin she set down by the reeds. The robe stayed hidden from the maiden. A content fairy wife with many children would still vanish into the lake if she regained her swanskin. The same held for seal-wives, the silkies, whose skin robes also needed concealment. Irish families like the Coneellys and the Flahertys claimed descent from such captured seal-wives.

okr.objective: Capturing fairies that can be held in Irish folklore.
key_results: Leprechauns could be caught by their shoulders.
Fairy women as swans were taken by stealing the swanskin robe.
A fairy wife vanished into the lake if she regained her robe.
Some Irish families claimed descent from captured seal-wives.
